structure.note: Schwab had voting common stock and nonvoting common stock, all of the nonvoting held by TD Bank. On February 12, 2025, TD sold its stake; its 31.7 million nonvoting shares converted into common stock on sale and the company repurchased the remaining 19.2 million, which also converted. From then on only voting common stock was outstanding. Charles R. Schwab, the founder and co-chairman, is the second-largest holder at 5.8%.

notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2024. Documents read on sec.gov: FY2024 Form 10-K (accession 0000316709-25-000010) and 2025 proxy statement (DEF 14A, accession 0001193125-25-072811). OWNERSHIP: 'Percent of Outstanding Shares' as of March 3, 2025. By then the nonvoting class had been eliminated: the 10-K cover shows only common stock (1,813,567,665 shares at February 12, 2025), so these percentages are effectively shares of all common stock. Charles R. Schwab's 105,262,153 shares include 930,316 he can acquire within 60 days, shares held by his spouse as trustee and by family limited partnerships, and 6,214,541 shares held by nonprofit public benefit corporations he established, for which he disclaims beneficial ownership. Family members' separate holdings, such as director Carolyn Schwab-Pomerantz's 2,132,067 shares, are not added. TD Bank, formerly a 5%+ holder, sold out on February 12, 2025. HOLDER asOf dates are the 13G/A filing dates the proxy cites. DIVIDENDS: the cash-flow 'Dividends paid' line ($2,275 million) combines common and preferred. The 10-K's dividend table reports cash paid on common and nonvoting common separately ($1,838 million), so that figure is used. Preferred dividends ($436.6 million in XBRL) are excluded. BUYBACKS: no common or nonvoting repurchases were made in 2024. The $1.5 billion repurchase of TD's nonvoting shares occurred on February 12, 2025, in fiscal 2025, and is not counted. GEOGRAPHY: null. Schwab reports two segments (Investor Services and Advisor Services) and the 10-K reviewed gives no revenue-by-geography table.

footprint.notes: Branches by state are not published: the FY2024 10-K says only that Schwab "had more than 380 domestic branch offices in 48 states and the District of Columbia, as well as locations in Puerto Rico, the United Kingdom, Hong Kong, and Singapore", and schwab.com's branch locator refused scripted requests (authorization error page). The Texas row is FDIC Summary of Deposits data (regulator tier, June 30, 2024) for Schwab's three FDIC-insured banks, each with one office, its main office in Westlake, TX; the FDIC therefore books all of their deposits to Texas, which says where the charters sit, not where depositors live. Values are kept per bank in $ thousands as the FDIC reports them (unit 'currency-thousands' is outside the lens enum, as in other footprint files) and are not added together. Sites are the 10-K Item 2 table of significant locations (square footage in thousands, net of subleased space); El Paso, TX (105,000 sq ft owned) and Richfield, OH (117,000 owned) are left out for the 12-site cap. [Editor] The FDIC rows are omitted from the map: all three banks book deposits at a single Westlake, Texas office, so a state map would show where the charters sit, not where clients are.
